source.title: Sparse but Wrong: Incorrect L0 Leads to Incorrect Features in Sparse Autoencoders

page_placements.theme: SAE and dictionary feature properties: interpretability scores, purity and stability vary by domain, layer and dictionary design (not neurons)

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on sparse-autoencoder latents and their dependence on SAE L0, but it does not audit model neurons or test the claim versions about neuron poles, neuron explanations, or neuron-based circuits.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern SAE feature mixing and SAE quality, not model neurons or their positive and negative poles. They are recorded as adjacent findings with versions ["none"]. The paper also mentions prior results from other work; those are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse autoencoders and measures how SAE latents mix features as L0 varies. It never audits a model's own neurons or neuron poles, analyses InceptionV1, builds neuron attribution graphs, or scores neuron explanations. It repeats the standard view that LLM neurons are polysemantic through superposition but tests nothing about it, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors conclude that L0 is not a neutral choice: too low or too high an L0 mixes correlated features into SAE latents. Sparsity–reconstruction plots are misleading, most open-source SAEs have L0 too low, and decoder pairwise cosine similarity can help choose L0 alongside downstream evaluations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains and evaluates SAEs while varying L0; it does not use the neuron-pole auditing or held-out neuron-explanation recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SAE feature-mixing patterns depend on L0; in the paper's comparison, high-L0 behavior also differs between BatchTopK and JumpReLU SAEs.

fits_no_version.finding: In toy models, SAE latents mix correlated features when L0 is too low or too high, and recover the true features at the correct L0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether SAE latents are monosemantic depends on setting L0 correctly; a wrong L0 yields polysemantic latents even when the underlying features are orthogonal.

fits_no_version.finding: With L0 set too low, a trained SAE whose latents are mixed reconstructs better than the ground-truth SAE (MSE 2.73 vs 4.88).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Plots of sparsity against reconstruction can favour SAEs that mix features.

fits_no_version.finding: Starting training at too low an L0 leaves lasting incorrect features even after L0 is corrected; starting too high recovers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature mixing caused by low L0 is a persistent local minimum.

fits_no_version.finding: The elbow in decoder pairwise cosine similarity (around L0 200) coincides with peak k=16 sparse-probing F1 in Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b SAEs. JumpReLU SAEs degrade less than BatchTopK at high L0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoder pairwise cosine similarity can help select the SAE L0 that gives the most monosemantic latents.

fits_no_version.finding: Most open-source SAEs on Neuronpedia report L0 below 100, against an estimated correct L0 of about 200–250 for Gemma-2-2b layer 12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Commonly used SAEs may have L0 set too low.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026), as stated in the text.
record.problems: The paper's evidence on SAE feature quality is limited to a few toy-model setups and a few LLM layers; its LLM experiments focus on BatchTopK and JumpReLU SAEs. Several reported outcomes are qualitative descriptions of plots rather than numeric estimates. These limitations do not turn the experiments into tests of neuron-pole interpretability.
record.rows_left_out: No additional main-text results bearing on the claim's neuron-pole versions were reported. Supplementary figure-only details without a textual result description, including the Gemma-2-2b layer 20 plots in Appendix J and detailed SAE histograms in Appendix K, were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles.
No neuron interpretability shares for any model; only SAEs are trained on Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b.
No vision models and no analysis of InceptionV1 neurons.
Shows that SAE latent quality depends on SAE architecture and L0, but does not measure model neuron interpretability across tools or architectures.
No neuron-based attribution graphs; no comparison of replacement-model reconstruction error.
No held-out prediction of neuron activations from explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study bears only indirectly on the essay's broader stance (tools matter for monosemanticity), and on SAEs, not neurons. It assumes that neuron polysemanticity comes from superposition rather than testing it. The appendix results not extracted as rows (Gemma layer 20; mixing as a function of correlation and of L0 in Appendix D; narrow-width and superposition-noise toy models) are also SAE-only and bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimates of the shares with one job, two jobs, or not-yet-understood jobs.
No audit of neuron-pole interpretability across dense or mixture-of-experts models or at trillion-parameter scale.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron analysis or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
Although SAE L0 is varied, the paper does not estimate the share of interpretable neurons, study InceptionV1-sized vision models, or compare neuron interpretability across architectures and tools.
No attribution-graph test of whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.
No test of whether explanations based on activating examples predict held-out neuron activations.
No scoring of neuron explanations by simulating their activations on new text.

relation.reason: It mentions polysemantic LLM neurons only as background motivation for SAEs. It does not test or use the claim.

tranche.reason: The paper studies how SAE L0 choice affects feature mixing in SAE latents. It neither tests nor uses any claim version about a model's own neurons.

source_check.notes: Results are on toy models and SAE L0 only (Gemma-2-2b SAEs, Neuronpedia L0 survey). There is no neuron-level evidence on any version, and all six rows are correctly linked to none.
